paragraphs.source_en: Besides this cicada-catching exercise, I also practise another exercise: pine-sliding. When I say pine-sliding, some may suppose I mean sliding down from a pine tree; in fact that is not so. This too is a kind of tree-climbing. The only difference is that in cicada-catching one climbs trees in order to catch cicadas, whereas in pine-sliding one climbs for the purpose of climbing itself. As for the pine, that evergreen tree, ever since Genemon is said to have entertained Hojo Tokiyori of Saimyoji by burning a precious old potted pine, its branches and trunk have remained to this day knotty and aged-looking. Consequently nothing is less slippery than a pine, and nothing is easier to grasp with paws and feet. In other words, nothing catches my claws so readily. I seek out just such a trunk, one that my claws can catch on easily, race up it in one breath, and then immediately race down again. There are two ways to race down: one is to descend with the head toward the ground, and the other is to keep the same posture as when climbing up and back down tail first. Here I should like to ask you human gentlemen: do you know which method is the more difficult? In the shallow judgment of human beings, you would surely think that since one is coming down, it must be easier to run down head first. But that is where you are wrong. You know that even Minamoto no Yoshitsune charged down the precipice at Hiyodorigoe head first, and so you suppose that a cat, of course, must come down head first too. You ought not to look down on cats in that way. In which direction do you suppose a cat's claws grow? Every one of them curves backward. Thus, like a fireman's hook, they can catch hold of things and pull them inward, but they are of little use for pushing things out in the opposite direction. Now suppose that I have nimbly raced up a pine tree. Since I am originally a creature of the ground, by the tendency of nature I am surely not permitted to remain long at the treetop. If I stay in the treetop for any length of time, I am bound to fall. Yet I have no wish simply to let go and fall, so I must adopt some means of moderating that natural tendency. That is why I must descend at once. Falling and climbing down appear to be very different, but in truth the difference is not so great as one imagines: slow down falling, and it becomes climbing down. Speed up climbing down, and it becomes falling; indeed falling and climbing down differ only by that one word, fall or climb. Naturally I do not care to fall from a pine tree, so I must slow down the fall and turn it into a descent. That is to say, I must somehow resist the speed of falling. As I have already informed you, all my claws point backward; if I keep my head up and set my claws into the trunk, the strength of those claws can be used against the force of the fall, and so falling is transformed into climbing down. It is a perfectly plain principle.

units.source_en: Besides this cicada-catching exercise, I also practise another exercise: pine-sliding.
units.source_zh: 除了这种捕蝉运动，我还搞另一种运动——“溜松”。

units.source_en: When I say pine-sliding, some may suppose I mean sliding down from a pine tree; in fact that is not so. This too is a kind of tree-climbing.

ja.t: れんが、そうではないやはり

units.source_zh: 一说到“溜松”，也许有人认为这是从松树上往下滑，其实不然，这也是爬树的一种。

units.source_en: The only difference is that in cicada-catching one climbs trees in order to catch cicadas, whereas in pine-sliding one climbs for the purpose of climbing itself.
units.source_zh: 只不过捕蝉运动是为了捉蝉才去爬树的，而“溜松”则是以爬树为目的而爬树，这就是两者之差。

units.source_en: As for the pine, that evergreen tree, ever since Genemon is said to have entertained Hojo Tokiyori of Saimyoji by burning a precious old potted pine, its branches and trunk have remained to this day knotty and aged-looking.

ja.t: るまで、いやにごつごつしている。

units.source_zh: 松树这种常青树，自从源右卫门不惜焚烧珍贵的盆景老松来款待出家最明寺的北条时赖以来，直到今天，它的枝干总是疙疙瘩瘩一副老态。

units.source_en: Consequently nothing is less slippery than a pine, and nothing is easier to grasp with paws and feet.
units.source_zh: 因此，再也没有比松树更不滑溜的了，再也没有比松树更容易用手脚抓住它的了。

units.source_en: In other words, nothing catches my claws so readily.
units.source_zh: 换句话说，也就是最容易挂住我的爪子的了。

units.source_en: I seek out just such a trunk, one that my claws can catch on easily, race up it in one breath, and then immediately race down again.
units.source_zh: 我就是找这种容易挂住爪子的树干，一口气飞跑上去，然后又马上飞跑下来。

units.source_en: There are two ways to race down: one is to descend with the head toward the ground, and the other is to keep the same posture as when climbing up and back down tail first.
units.source_zh: 往下飞跑的时候有两种方法可供选择，一是头朝着地面爬下来，一是仍保持向上爬的姿势，尾巴朝下退下来。

units.source_en: Here I should like to ask you human gentlemen: do you know which method is the more difficult?

ja.t: うがどっちがむずかしいか

units.source_zh: 我在这里倒要请问一下人类诸君，你们知道哪种方法最难吗？

units.source_en: In the shallow judgment of human beings, you would surely think that since one is coming down, it must be easier to run down head first.
units.source_zh: 按人类的浅薄想法，一定会认为既然要下来，当然是头朝下跑下来比较容易。

units.source_en: But that is where you are wrong.
units.source_zh: 其实这就错了。

units.source_en: You know that even Minamoto no Yoshitsune charged down the precipice at Hiyodorigoe head first, and so you suppose that a cat, of course, must come down head first too.
units.source_zh: 你们知道连源义经也是头朝下从“鹎越”山路的悬崖绝壁上跳下去的，所以以为猫儿当然是头朝下下来的。

units.source_en: You ought not to look down on cats in that way.
units.source_zh: 你们这样看不起猫是不应该的。

units.source_en: In which direction do you suppose a cat's claws grow?
units.source_zh: 你们认为猫爪是朝哪个方向长着的？

units.source_en: Every one of them curves backward.
units.source_zh: 所有的爪子都是向后弯曲的呀。

units.source_en: Thus, like a fireman's hook, they can catch hold of things and pull them inward, but they are of little use for pushing things out in the opposite direction.
units.source_zh: 这样，它就像“消防钩”一样，能够钩住东西，往里拉过来，但用它把东西往相反的方向推出去，却不太管用了。

units.source_en: Now suppose that I have nimbly raced up a pine tree. Since I am originally a creature of the ground, by the tendency of nature I am surely not permitted to remain long at the treetop.
units.source_zh: 现在，假定我轻快地爬上松树，然而我原是地上的动物，从自然的倾向来说，肯定不允许长期留在树梢上。

units.source_en: If I stay in the treetop for any length of time, I am bound to fall.
units.source_zh: 如果在树梢上多待一些工夫那就必然会摔下来。

units.source_en: Yet I have no wish simply to let go and fall, so I must adopt some means of moderating that natural tendency.

ja.t: かゆるめなければならん。

units.source_zh: 然而我并不想就这样一松手摔下去，因此必须采取某种手段来缓和这种自然倾向。

units.source_en: That is why I must descend at once.
units.source_zh: 这就是为什么我必须立即爬下来。

units.source_en: Falling and climbing down appear to be very different, but in truth the difference is not so great as one imagines: slow down falling, and it becomes climbing down.
units.source_zh: 摔下来与爬下来似乎有很大的差别，其实并不像想象的那样有很大的不同，将“摔下来”放慢，就会变成“爬下来”。

units.source_en: Speed up climbing down, and it becomes falling; indeed falling and climbing down differ only by that one word, fall or climb.
units.source_zh: 将“爬下来”加快，就会变成“摔下来”，摔下来与爬下来，其实只不过是“摔”与“爬”的一字之差而已。

units.source_en: Naturally I do not care to fall from a pine tree, so I must slow down the fall and turn it into a descent.
units.source_zh: 我当然不愿意从松树上摔下来，所以必须将“摔下来”放慢变为“爬下来”。

units.source_en: That is to say, I must somehow resist the speed of falling.
units.source_zh: 也就是说必须用某种办法来缓解摔下来的速度。

units.source_en: As I have already informed you, all my claws point backward; if I keep my head up and set my claws into the trunk, the strength of those claws can be used against the force of the fall, and so falling is transformed into climbing down.
units.source_zh: 正如刚才已经奉告各位的那样，在下的爪子都是朝后长着的，如果采用头朝上的姿势，用爪子抓住树干，那么，这爪子的力度却可以逆用往下落的劲儿，于是就可以变“摔下来”为“爬下来”。

units.source_en: It is a perfectly plain principle.
units.source_zh: 这是个很容易明白的道理。

paragraphs.source_zh: 除了这种捕蝉运动，我还搞另一种运动——“溜松”。一说到“溜松”，也许有人认为这是从松树上往下滑，其实不然，这也是爬树的一种。只不过捕蝉运动是为了捉蝉才去爬树的，而“溜松”则是以爬树为目的而爬树，这就是两者之差。松树这种常青树，自从源右卫门不惜焚烧珍贵的盆景老松来款待出家最明寺的北条时赖以来，直到今天，它的枝干总是疙疙瘩瘩一副老态。因此，再也没有比松树更不滑溜的了，再也没有比松树更容易用手脚抓住它的了。换句话说，也就是最容易挂住我的爪子的了。我就是找这种容易挂住爪子的树干，一口气飞跑上去，然后又马上飞跑下来。往下飞跑的时候有两种方法可供选择，一是头朝着地面爬下来，一是仍保持向上爬的姿势，尾巴朝下退下来。我在这里倒要请问一下人类诸君，你们知道哪种方法最难吗？按人类的浅薄想法，一定会认为既然要下来，当然是头朝下跑下来比较容易。其实这就错了。你们知道连源义经也是头朝下从“鹎越”山路的悬崖绝壁上跳下去的，所以以为猫儿当然是头朝下下来的。你们这样看不起猫是不应该的。你们认为猫爪是朝哪个方向长着的？所有的爪子都是向后弯曲的呀。这样，它就像“消防钩”一样，能够钩住东西，往里拉过来，但用它把东西往相反的方向推出去，却不太管用了。现在，假定我轻快地爬上松树，然而我原是地上的动物，从自然的倾向来说，肯定不允许长期留在树梢上。如果在树梢上多待一些工夫那就必然会摔下来。然而我并不想就这样一松手摔下去，因此必须采取某种手段来缓和这种自然倾向。这就是为什么我必须立即爬下来。摔下来与爬下来似乎有很大的差别，其实并不像想象的那样有很大的不同，将“摔下来”放慢，就会变成“爬下来”。将“爬下来”加快，就会变成“摔下来”，摔下来与爬下来，其实只不过是“摔”与“爬”的一字之差而已。我当然不愿意从松树上摔下来，所以必须将“摔下来”放慢变为“爬下来”。也就是说必须用某种办法来缓解摔下来的速度。正如刚才已经奉告各位的那样，在下的爪子都是朝后长着的，如果采用头朝上的姿势，用爪子抓住树干，那么，这爪子的力度却可以逆用往下落的劲儿，于是就可以变“摔下来”为“爬下来”。这是个很容易明白的道理。

paragraphs.source_en: However, you may try it if you like: turn yourself upside down and attempt pine-sliding in Yoshitsune's cliff-descending style. Then, though you have claws, they will be of no use at all; you will merely slip and slide downward, unable anywhere to support your own weight. Thus, though your intention was to climb down, the result changes into falling. From this one sees that the Hiyodorigoe cliff method is exceedingly difficult. Among cats, probably I alone possess this accomplishment. That is precisely why I call this exercise pine-sliding.

units.source_en: However, you may try it if you like: turn yourself upside down and attempt pine-sliding in Yoshitsune's cliff-descending style.
units.source_zh: 然而，你也不妨试试，如果头朝下，采取源义经跳悬崖的办法，也来个“溜松”。

units.source_en: Then, though you have claws, they will be of no use at all; you will merely slip and slide downward, unable anywhere to support your own weight.
units.source_zh: 那么虽有爪子也一点派不上用场，只会哧溜哧溜往下滑，根本无法支持自身的重量。

units.source_en: Thus, though your intention was to climb down, the result changes into falling.

ja.t: ここにおいてかせっかく

units.source_zh: 于是尽管本意是想“爬下来”结果一变而为“摔下来”。

units.source_en: From this one sees that the Hiyodorigoe cliff method is exceedingly difficult.
units.source_zh: 可见，跳“鹎越”悬崖的办法实在太难了。

units.source_en: Among cats, probably I alone possess this accomplishment.
units.source_zh: 在猫儿当中能有这种伎俩的，恐怕只有我一个啦。

units.source_en: That is precisely why I call this exercise pine-sliding.
units.source_zh: 正因为如此，我才将这个运动称作“溜松”的啊。

paragraphs.source_zh: 然而，你也不妨试试，如果头朝下，采取源义经跳悬崖的办法，也来个“溜松”。那么虽有爪子也一点派不上用场，只会哧溜哧溜往下滑，根本无法支持自身的重量。于是尽管本意是想“爬下来”结果一变而为“摔下来”。可见，跳“鹎越”悬崖的办法实在太难了。在猫儿当中能有这种伎俩的，恐怕只有我一个啦。正因为如此，我才将这个运动称作“溜松”的啊。
